note: Captured with tests/test_watchdog.py's RT-27 additions present and deploy/nightshift-watchdog.sh UNMODIFIED at the wave-2 checkpoint (git diff --name-only deploy/ was empty at capture time). exit_code 1 => derived kind 'regression'. COUNT CORRECTED, see `correction` below: the true baseline split is 5 pass / 3 fail, NOT 4 pass / 4 fail. Of the 5 that pass, 4 are the fail-closed guards (a recorded run with no beat still alerts, an unreadable plane still alerts, non-'missing' reasons are never graced, the alive path asks no second question), which must hold both before and after and are what stop this fix degenerating into 'delete the missing alert'. The 5th, test_rt27_never_started_box_does_not_burn_the_realert_window, passes VACUOUSLY and is evidence of nothing in either direction -- it is disclosed here rather than counted.
correction: Issue #57. The original note claimed '4 of 8 assertions fail pre-fix; the 4 that pass are the fail-closed guards'. Re-running the SHIPPED tests against this same baseline_sha gives `Ran 8 tests ... FAILED (failures=3)`. Two things were wrong. (1) THE COUNT: 3 of 8 fail, so the split is 5/3. (2) THE VACUOUS PASS: the assertion that flipped, test_rt27_never_started_box_does_not_burn_the_realert_window, does not pass because the baseline script left the re-alert window unburned -- it passes because the harness looks in the wrong place. Box.marker_exists() resolves $HOME/.config/omnigent/watchdog-last-alert (the POST-F2 path), while Box.run() sets XDG_STATE_HOME to a deliberate decoy and the baseline script resolves STATE_DIR="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/omnigent". MEASURED against this baseline: the box DID alert (alert_count == 1) and the marker WAS written, to $XDG_STATE_HOME/omnigent/watchdog-last-alert in the decoy; marker_exists() returned False anyway, so assertFalse passed. The re-alert window was burned; only the assertion's gaze missed it. RT-27.txt's verbatim block is the ORIGINAL capture, taken against the pre-F2 harness where marker_exists() still read the XDG path, and it is left byte-for-byte intact as an archive; the header prepended to that file carries the same correction. Nobody should count this assertion as pre-fix evidence.
